thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple nodes in kube-infer-prod are transitioning to NotReady (eu-west-1). 5xx spike on /v1/generate and increased pod evictions. Paging oncall.
sam.sre: got it, I'm on pager. Which pool is hit?
priya.runtime: looks like gpu-infer-pool-a and gpu-infer-pool-b. Grafana shows kubelet heartbeat drops and node Ready -> NotReady flapping.
sam.sre: copy. Nina, any customer tickets? 
nina.support: two customers reporting timeouts, one is high priority. I've notified account team.
jorge.infra: pulling node list now. run: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference -o wide`
priya.runtime: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide` shows many pods in CrashLoopBackOff and Terminating. Also seeing `NVRM: Xid` logs on a couple of nodes (possible GPU driver/kernel issue).
sam.sre: can you paste the node describe / kubelet logs? also check `dmesg | grep -i oom` and `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200`.
priya.runtime: pasted snippet:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:07:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679012] Kernel panic - not syncing: Out of memory
```
and kubelet shows repeated `Node status: NotReady - kubelet not responding`.
jorge.infra: I see a recent node-agent-daemonset rollout ~40m ago from deploy-bot. Deploy-bot, any noise?
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T09:14:22 - node-agent v2.4.1 rolled to eu-west-1 inference pool. No automated rollback.
sam.sre: possible relation but let's not assume. Immediate mitigations: 1) cordon the most flappy nodes 2) scale up fallback CPU-only pool and route low-priority traffic 3) remove affected nodes from service with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data <node>` (careful with live inference pods)
leah.se: I can update routing rules for non-urgent models to fallback-model-cpu, on it.
priya.runtime: recommending temporary kubelet restart on the affected nodes: `systemctl restart kubelet` after cordon, and don't drain until kubelet stable.
sam.sre: Jorge, can you check kernel/kernel-driver versions and if there's a known nvidia-driver bug? also open support ticket with cloud provider if we see `GPU fell off the bus`.
jorge.infra: opening ticket now. Also toggling OOM killer logs retention for the nodes.
nina.support: posted customer-facing note to incident channel and support queue. ETA communicated as ~30-45m while we stabilize.
oncall-backup: I'm ready to take over if you need to rotate. what's the handoff plan?
sam.sre: I'll stay until we have stable state, then handoff. Current status: cordoned 4 nodes, restarted kubelet on 3, scale-up added 6 cpu-worker nodes, traffic reroute in progress. 5xx rate down from 8% to 1.2% over last 6 min.
priya.runtime: after kubelet restarts, two nodes came back Ready but GPU errors persist on one node. We removed it from the cluster and powered cycle via cloud console.
jorge.infra: cloud support acknowledged possible host-level GPU fault and is performing hardware remediation.
leah.se: customer updates sent. No SLA breach expected if we maintain current pace.
sam.sre: next steps: keep monitoring, keep fallback routing until we validate node health for 2x 10m windows, escalate to platform if further GPU HW errors. create postmortem ticket `PM-2026-03-15-node-flip` and assign.
priya.runtime: saving logs to s3: `s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2012345678/` and marking snapshot for affected nodes.
nina.support: adding affected customer IDs to the incident ticket.
oncall-backup: acknowledged, will take over if you need rest. Good work team :thumbsup:
sam.sre: handing off at 2012347230 to oncall-backup. If anything critical, page pager again. Incident channel for postmortem: #incidents. Closing live mitigation thread.
incident-bot: Incident update: severity -> P1 (partial degraded) -> reduced impact. Follow-up: create PM, RCA, and timeline.
